rows.evidence: Q1: Sections II-III, field experiment at Chott Meriem, Tunisia, April-June 2011, cucumber under drip lines at 0, 15 and 30 cm depth with TDR soil moisture, yield and WUE measured. Q2: Section 3.5 and Fig. 8, WUE highest in T2 (15 kg m-3), about 20% and 13% higher than T1 and T0; Section 3.1 and Fig. 4, soil water stock 10.2% greater in T1 than T0, interpreted as weaker evaporation losses under subsurface placement; Abstract/Conclusion state SDI minimises evaporative loss and increases use efficiency. Q4: Sections 2.2 and 3.1-3.2, Figs 3-5, soil water stock and its day-to-day variation measured daily by TDR (gravimetrically calibrated) under each dripline depth, the intermediate variable linking SSDI to reduced evaporation/drainage and WUE.
rows.notes: Evaporation and deep seepage were not measured directly; they are inferred from the soil water stock differences (drainage losses for T2 only asserted). WUE differences between treatments were reported as not statistically significant, though yield differences were. Single site, single crop, single season, 212 m2 plot. Q3 no: TDR soil water and yield-based WUE are different outcomes, not two independent methods for one result. Q7 doubtful: authors say a 30 cm depth is probably acceptable on their soil type and climate when the crop is fully irrigated, but this is hedged and not stated as a requirement; the 'proper depth' condition is cited from [11]. Q8 doubtful: restriction to 'our soil type and climate' and the remark that soil water content is an imperfect indicator of plant water status (partly copied from literature) are borderline; closing 'further observations needed' is generic. Q9: only means and SNK letters, no SD/SE/CI given in text.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections II-III, own field experiment on cucumber under surface and subsurface drip at three depths with soil water, leaf area, yield and WUE measurements.
rows.notes: The study contains no observation or measurement of weeds or any pest; it reports only soil water stock, leaf area, yield and WUE under drip lines at 0, 15 and 30 cm depth. It provides no evidence on weed growth reduction by SSDI.

notes: Text appears complete though figures are not reproduced; some discussion sentences (e.g. references to maize/corn and 'They recommend') seem copied from other work, which makes attribution of some statements to the authors' own findings uncertain.
